overview: This Senate resolution congratulates Texas A&M University on 150 years of service, marked on October 4, 2026, the anniversary of its first day of classes in 1876. It recounts the school's founding as Texas's first public college under the federal land-grant program, which gave states public land to fund colleges for agriculture, engineering and military training. It highlights the university's long military tradition, including the large numbers of graduates who served in World Wars I and II, along with its traditions, research, athletics and more than 653,000 graduates. It asks that copies be sent to the university's president, chancellor and board chairman. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on September 30, 2026.
for: Supporters say the resolution fittingly honors a major public university's long record of education, research and military service.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic: it does not change any law or provide any funding.
